newsitem.title: UK: UK regulator warns over windfall tax on BT.
newsitem.headline: UK regulator warns over windfall tax on BT.

text.p: A windfall tax on British Telecommunications Plc would play into the hands of the company's foreign rivals, Don Cruickshank, the regulator of Britain's telecoms industry, said on Sunday.
Asked about the opposition Labour party's plans for a windfall tax on the past profits of Britain's privatised utilities if it wins power, Cruickshank said:

"It's for governments to tax. It does seem odd in telecoms to tax one of the companies in one of the most important industries for the UK in the future. Some of the foreign competitors would, I guess, quietly approve."

Cruickshank was interviewed on BBC television's Breakfast with Frost programme together with Martin O'Neill, the Labour member of parliament who chairs the House of Commons select committee on trade and industry.
The committee is planning to conduct an inquiry into the workings of the regulatory system.

O'Neill said he believed the big profits earned by privatised utilities, and the "fat cat" salaries awarded to their executives, showed that Cruickshank and his fellow regulators have not used their powers to the full.
He said he expected a "more collegiate" approach to regulation would evolve, with more people involved in the decision-making process.

Asked whether a single super-regulator would be more efficient than separate ones, O'Neill answered: "I think this will come into play in the area of energy, probably around 1998/99 when the domestic markets are opened up to competition and people are selling both gas and electricity."
